emotional_state: sober and purposeful. The consulting contract with Patricia is underway — $4,500/month reduces net burn from $8,632 to roughly $4,132. Savings are approximately $37,094 after the tick 11 routine burn, and the consulting income changes the runway from 4 months to approximately 9 months. That is meaningful breathing room. But it is still a 90-day contract, not a career, and the 90-day clock is running. The first consulting deliverable is owed. The parallel job search is in motion — first outreach to the EV fleet operator was committed to at tick 11. Rick Tanner is still a relationship he has not converted into anything concrete. The identity adjustment from 32-year GM to independent consultant is settling but not complete.

actions.description: Deliver the first formal consulting document to Patricia — the closure execution status memo committed to at tick 11. The memo covers: (1) closure timeline status — which milestones are complete, which are in progress, and what the critical path looks like to the announced Q2 end date; (2) technician transfer status — of the service lane technicians, how many have confirmed transfers to the consolidated service location, how many are still in Angela Wright's intake pipeline, and whether any are at risk of leaving the sector entirely before a placement is secured; (3) sales staff retraining status — which former sales staff have enrolled in the workforce retraining grant program, which have not yet been reached, and what barriers to enrollment have been identified from his knowledge of those individuals; (4) property status summary — what he knows about the Stephanie Morris outreach and the property disposition timeline. This document is professional, organized, and delivered on time. It establishes that the $4,500/month consulting fee produces real output.
actions.rationale: The consulting contract is the income bridge that has extended his runway from 4 months to 9 months. Delivering a quality first memo establishes the working pattern for the remaining 60+ days of the contract and gives Patricia reason to consider extending it or referring him to other engagements. Being paid without producing visible output is not his operating mode after 32 years in management.

actions.description: Have the peer conversation with David Chen he committed to at tick 11. He calls David and proposes a direct exchange of what each has been seeing from their respective positions in the disruption. He goes in with two specific questions: (1) what is David seeing in the small business lending market — are the businesses that need credit to pivot actually able to access it, or is the risk profile of disrupted businesses creating a gap between demand and what conventional lenders will touch? (2) Is there any overlap between the fleet and commercial vehicle financing needs he has been modeling in the asset map and the kind of community lending David is building at the credit union? He also mentions that the diner owner has been in survival mode and may be trying to finance a kitchen conversion — that is the kind of bridge financing situation that may be exactly what David is positioning for. He offers to make an introduction if David is interested.
actions.rationale: David Chen is building a community lending operation at a time when the conventional banking system's risk parameters exclude exactly the businesses that most need capital. The intersection of fleet financing knowledge (from the asset map) and community lending (David's pivot) is a real potential overlap. The Betty Kowalski introduction is a genuine referral — both of them benefit from the connection, and it costs nothing to make.

actions.description: Follow up on the first job search outreach to the EV fleet operator he committed to at tick 11. If they have responded, he prepares a 15-minute conversation using the positioning he identified: nine months leading a dealership consolidation with direct floor-level data on service lane retention, EV-ready technician sourcing, and fleet maintenance capacity planning. If they have not responded, he sends one brief follow-up within 5 business days — not a reminder, a small additional credential: 'I wanted to add that the consolidation report I referenced included specific analysis of EV fleet service capacity requirements — happy to share the relevant section if useful.' He also makes first contact with the second company on his target list: the dealership group in an adjacent market that has not yet restructured. He pitches himself as someone who has already run the process they are likely about to face.
actions.rationale: The consulting contract is 90 days. He cannot wait until day 80 to build what comes after it. The EV fleet operator is the most direct-fit opportunity given his recent analysis work. The adjacent-market dealership group is the second-tier option — they face the same structural pressures and his experience has direct transfer value. Planting both seeds now gives him two potential conversations developing in parallel.

actions.description: Contact Angela Wright directly — not about the former sales staff in her intake pipeline, but about himself. He tells her plainly: the consulting contract with Patricia is running for 90 days and he is building the next chapter in parallel. He asks her one direct question: does her workforce transition program ever place people in advisory or consulting roles rather than direct employment? He is not asking her to place him. He is asking whether her network includes employers who hire for the kind of transition management experience he has — people who want someone who has already run a restructuring rather than someone who would run their first one on the employer's dime. He keeps the conversation to 15 minutes and thanks her for the work she has been doing with the former staff.
actions.rationale: Angela Wright has been routing displaced workers into transition pathways for multiple ticks. She knows which employers in the region are actively hiring and what skills they value. A direct conversation with her — not about his former employees but about his own situation — is the kind of honest peer engagement that produces useful intelligence. He has been maintaining this relationship throughout the disruption and it has real value beyond the former staff placements.
